spider-lunge-with-rotation.name: Spider Lunge with Rotation
spider-lunge-with-rotation.execution: From a plank, step one foot to the outside of the same-side hand into a deep lunge, back leg long and hips low. Reach the inside arm under and through, then rotate it up toward the ceiling, opening the chest and following the hand with your eyes. Return the hand down and step back to plank. Alternate sides.
spider-lunge-with-rotation.why: Dynamically loads the lead-leg hip flexors and adductors into deep flexion while the rotation mobilizes the thoracic spine and lengthens the obliques, raising tissue temperature and joint range before loading.
spider-lunge-with-rotation.transfer: Prepares the deep hip and groin range used in the wide stride and crossovers, and the t-spine rotation needed to wind up into shots; reduces early-session groin/hip strain risk.
spider-lunge-with-rotation.cues: "Drop the back hip" · "reach tall, eyes follow the hand" · "long spine, not crunched"
spider-lunge-with-rotation.mistakes: Rushing the rotation; back knee bouncing on the floor; rounding the low back instead of rotating the t-spine
spider-lunge-with-rotation.progression: Progress: 2-sec hold at end range | Regress: drop the back knee for support
spider-lunge-with-rotation.muscles: Hip flexors, adductors, glutes, thoracic erectors, obliques

inchworm-to-push-up.name: Inchworm to Push-Up
inchworm-to-push-up.execution: Stand tall, hinge at the hips and place hands on the floor (bend knees as needed). Walk the hands out to a plank, core braced and hips level. Perform one push-up, then walk the hands back toward the feet and stand to finish. Move smoothly and control each phase.
inchworm-to-push-up.why: Combines a dynamic posterior-chain stretch on the walk-out with full-body tension and a push-up, elevating core temperature and grooving plank stability and scapular control before training.
inchworm-to-push-up.transfer: Primes hamstring length and anterior-core bracing used in a low skating posture, and builds the pressing/scapular stability that supports puck protection and absorbing contact.
inchworm-to-push-up.cues: "Brace before you walk out" · "hips don’t sag" · "slow the hands, not your breath"
inchworm-to-push-up.mistakes: Hips sagging or piking in plank; locking knees and straining the low back; bouncing through the push-up
inchworm-to-push-up.progression: Progress: add a shoulder tap at plank | Regress: omit the push-up, walk out and back
inchworm-to-push-up.muscles: Hamstrings, anterior core, shoulders, chest, triceps

lateral-squat-shift.name: Lateral Squat Shift
lateral-squat-shift.execution: Stand wide, toes mostly forward. Shift weight to one side, bending that knee and pushing the hips back while the opposite leg stays straight. Both heels down, chest tall. Sink to a comfortable depth, feel the straight-leg adductor stretch, then glide smoothly to the other side. Stay low throughout.
lateral-squat-shift.why: Actively lengthens the straight-leg adductors while loading the bent-leg hip into flexion and abduction, opening frontal-plane hip range and waking the inner-thigh and glute musculature for lateral work.
lateral-squat-shift.transfer: Directly prepares the side-to-side push of the stride and crossovers; mobile, switched-on adductors improve push-off and lower the risk of the groin strains that plague skaters.
lateral-squat-shift.cues: "Heels stay down" · "push hips back, not knees forward" · "stay low, glide across"
lateral-squat-shift.mistakes: Heel lifting on the bent side; rounding forward at the chest; staying too shallow to gain range
lateral-squat-shift.progression: Progress: light goblet load or 2-sec pause each side | Regress: hold a pole for balance, reduce depth

a-skip-in-place.name: A-Skip in Place
a-skip-in-place.execution: Standing tall, skip in place driving one knee to hip height while the opposite arm drives forward in a 1-2 rhythm. Stay on the balls of the feet, dorsiflex the lifted ankle (toe up), and strike the ground actively under the hip. Keep posture upright and the rhythm crisp.
a-skip-in-place.why: Grooves the coordinated arm-leg sprint rhythm, reinforces dorsiflexion and a stiff, reactive ankle, and primes the stretch-shortening cycle and rate of force development in the lower leg at low intensity.
a-skip-in-place.transfer: Reinforces the knee-drive, ankle stiffness, and arm action that transfer to off-ice acceleration mechanics and stride recovery; an effective primer before sprint or jump work.
a-skip-in-place.cues: "Tall and tight" · "toe up, strike under the hip" · "punch the arms"
a-skip-in-place.mistakes: Reaching the foot out in front; collapsing posture; lazy or mistimed arm swing
a-skip-in-place.progression: Progress: A-skip moving for distance | Regress: marching in place with knee drive
a-skip-in-place.muscles: Hip flexors, calves, glutes, anterior tibialis

90-90-hip-switch.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
90-90-hip-switch.execution: Sit with one leg bent in front (shin across, 90°) and the other bent to the side (90°), both knees down. Chest tall, lift the knees and rotate the hips to switch to the mirror position on the other side. Control the rotation through the hips, not by hiking the spine. Alternate smoothly.
90-90-hip-switch.why: Trains active internal and external hip rotation through a large range under control, improving rotary hip mobility and the ability to access end-range positions without compensating from the lumbar spine.
90-90-hip-switch.transfer: Builds the hip rotation range needed for tight turns, opening the hips on crossovers, and rotating into shots; better rotary mobility protects the low back and hips during quick directional changes.
90-90-hip-switch.cues: "Move from the hips, not the back" · "stay tall through the switch" · "knees lead, controlled"
90-90-hip-switch.mistakes: Leaning back and rounding to force the switch; rushing through range; chest collapsing
90-90-hip-switch.progression: Progress: hands off the floor / lean over the front shin | Regress: assist with hands, reduce range

jumping-jacks.name: Jumping Jacks
jumping-jacks.execution: Stand tall, feet together, arms at sides. Jump the feet out wide while sweeping the arms overhead, then jump back as the arms return. Land softly on the balls of the feet with soft knees and keep a steady, rhythmic pace. Breathe rhythmically for the prescribed time.
jumping-jacks.why: A low-skill, full-body raiser that increases core temperature, heart rate, and blood flow while rehearsing soft, rhythmic landings and limb abduction/adduction to prepare for higher-intensity work.
jumping-jacks.transfer: A general warm-up raiser that elevates readiness before a session; the repeated soft landings lightly prime the ankle and knee elasticity used in skating and jumping.
jumping-jacks.mistakes: Stiff, heavy landings; half-range arms; holding the breath
jumping-jacks.progression: Progress: seal jacks or faster tempo | Regress: step-out jacks (no jump)

high-knees.name: High Knees
high-knees.execution: Run in place (or moving) driving the knees to hip height in a quick, rhythmic cadence. Stay tall on the balls of the feet, dorsiflex the ankles, and drive the arms in opposition. Keep ground contacts short and snappy and posture upright. Continue for the prescribed time.
high-knees.why: Elevates heart rate while rehearsing fast ground contacts, high knee drive, and reciprocal arm action, priming hip-flexor turnover and reactive ankle stiffness for sprint and skating mechanics.
high-knees.transfer: Reinforces the rapid knee recovery and turnover that translate to stride frequency in off-ice acceleration; an efficient cardiovascular and neuromuscular primer before speed work.
high-knees.cues: "Knees to hip height" · "quick, light contacts" · "tall posture"
high-knees.mistakes: Leaning back; slow, heavy feet; arms not driving
high-knees.progression: Progress: high knees for distance at higher cadence | Regress: marching high knees
high-knees.muscles: Hip flexors, calves, anterior tibialis, glutes

butt-kicks.name: Butt Kicks
butt-kicks.execution: Jog in place or move forward, flicking the heels up toward the glutes with a quick hamstring contraction. Stay tall on the balls of the feet with short ground contacts and let the arms swing in rhythm. Keep the knees pointing down and the cadence quick.
butt-kicks.why: Dynamically activates the hamstrings through rapid knee flexion and rehearses fast leg recovery, raising tissue temperature and priming the posterior chain and ankle elasticity before sprinting.
butt-kicks.transfer: Primes the hamstring and leg-recovery action used in stride return; warms the posterior chain to reduce early hamstring tightness before higher-intensity skating-pattern or sprint work.
butt-kicks.cues: "Heels to glutes, fast" · "stay on the balls of the feet" · "tall and quick"
butt-kicks.mistakes: Knees swinging forward; leaning at the waist; slow turnover
butt-kicks.progression: Progress: butt kicks moving at higher cadence | Regress: slower alternating heel flicks

banded-clamshell.name: Banded Clamshell
banded-clamshell.execution: Side-lying, hips and knees bent ~45°, mini-band above the knees, feet stacked. Keeping feet together and pelvis stable (don’t roll back), lift the top knee against the band by rotating from the hip. Pause at the top, then lower with control. Complete reps, then switch sides.
banded-clamshell.why: Isolates the gluteus medius and deep external hip rotators, building frontal-plane hip control and the strength to resist knee collapse — key stabilizers that are often weak and underused.
banded-clamshell.transfer: Strengthens the glute med that controls hip and knee alignment during single-leg push-off and crossovers; better lateral hip stability improves edge control and protects the knee and groin.
banded-clamshell.cues: "Pelvis stays still" · "open from the hip, not the low back" · "feet glued together"
banded-clamshell.mistakes: Rolling the pelvis back to cheat range; using momentum; top foot drifting apart
banded-clamshell.progression: Progress: heavier band or isometric hold at top | Regress: lighter/no band, smaller range
banded-clamshell.muscles: Gluteus medius, deep hip external rotators

banded-lateral-walk.name: Banded Lateral Walk
banded-lateral-walk.execution: Mini-band above knees or ankles. Drop into a quarter-squat athletic stance with band tension. Step one foot out to the side, then bring the trailing foot part-way in — keep constant tension. Stay low, chest up, toes forward. Travel a set number of steps each direction.
banded-lateral-walk.why: Keeps the gluteus medius under continuous tension while resisting hip adduction and knee valgus, building the lateral-hip strength and stability that controls the knee and pelvis during side-to-side movement.
banded-lateral-walk.transfer: Directly strengthens the abduction/lateral-push pattern of skating and crossovers; a switched-on glute med improves push-off power and edge stability while protecting the knee from caving.
banded-lateral-walk.cues: "Stay low the whole way" · "lead with the heel, toes forward" · "keep band tension"
banded-lateral-walk.mistakes: Standing tall between steps; knees caving in; feet snapping together (losing tension)
banded-lateral-walk.progression: Progress: heavier band or lower stance | Regress: lighter band, fewer steps
banded-lateral-walk.muscles: Gluteus medius, glute max, hip abductors

world-s-greatest-stretch.name: World's Greatest Stretch
world-s-greatest-stretch.execution: From standing, step into a deep forward lunge and place both hands inside the front foot. Drop the back-side elbow toward the floor near the front foot, then rotate the front-side arm up toward the ceiling, opening the chest. Reverse the rotation, straighten the front leg briefly, then step back and switch.
world-s-greatest-stretch.why: A multi-joint sequence that mobilizes hip flexors, adductors, hamstrings, and thoracic spine in one flow, opening the major ranges used in athletic positions and raising tissue temperature efficiently.
world-s-greatest-stretch.transfer: Opens the deep hip, groin, and t-spine ranges needed for the wide stride, crossovers, and rotating into shots; a time-efficient prep that reduces early-session stiffness and strain risk.
world-s-greatest-stretch.cues: "Sink the hips low" · "reach tall and open the chest" · "control, don’t bounce"
world-s-greatest-stretch.mistakes: Shallow lunge; rotating from the low back instead of the t-spine; rushing the sequence
world-s-greatest-stretch.progression: Progress: longer end-range hold on the reach | Regress: hands on a low box, reduce depth
world-s-greatest-stretch.muscles: Hip flexors, adductors, hamstrings, thoracic spine, glutes

t-spine-rotation.name: T-Spine Rotation
t-spine-rotation.execution: In quadruped or half-kneeling, place one hand behind the head. Rotate that elbow down and under toward the opposite arm, then open it up and back toward the ceiling, following the elbow with your eyes. Keep the hips square and the movement from the upper back, not the lumbar spine. Switch sides.
t-spine-rotation.why: Improves thoracic rotation range while keeping the lumbar spine stable, restoring the upper-back mobility that lets rotation occur where it should rather than overloading the low back.
t-spine-rotation.transfer: Builds the t-spine rotation that powers wrist and slap shot wind-up and follow-through; keeping the lumbar stable while rotating from the upper back protects the low back during shooting and checking.
t-spine-rotation.cues: "Hips square, turn the upper back" · "follow the elbow with your eyes" · "open the chest"
t-spine-rotation.mistakes: Rotating from the lower back/hips; rushing reps; limited end range
t-spine-rotation.progression: Progress: exhale and 2-sec hold at end range | Regress: smaller range, slower tempo

adductor-rocker.name: Adductor Rocker
adductor-rocker.execution: On hands and knees, extend one leg straight out to the side, foot flat and toes forward, hips level. Sit the hips back toward the bent-leg heel, feeling a stretch through the straight leg’s inner thigh, then rock forward. Keep a flat back, move slowly. Repeat, then switch sides.
adductor-rocker.why: Loads the extended-leg adductors through a controlled dynamic stretch while the rocking gradually increases tolerable range, improving groin mobility under low load.
adductor-rocker.transfer: Prepares and lengthens the adductors/groin heavily loaded in the wide stride and crossovers; improving this range is a key strategy to reduce the common groin/hip strains in skaters.
adductor-rocker.cues: "Flat back, hips level" · "toes forward, foot flat" · "rock slow, no bounce"
adductor-rocker.mistakes: Rounding the back; bouncing into range; foot rolling / toes pointing up
adductor-rocker.progression: Progress: increase range or brief end-range hold | Regress: smaller range, less rock-back

ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion (Wall)
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.execution: Half-kneeling or staggered stance facing a wall, front foot a few inches away. Keeping the heel flat, drive the front knee forward over the toes toward the wall without the heel lifting. Touch the knee to the wall if able, then return. Move the foot back to progress. Reps per side.
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.why: Improves ankle dorsiflexion by repeatedly loading the joint into flexion with the heel anchored, lengthening the calf and improving the talus glide that limits squat and stride depth when restricted.
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.transfer: Restores the ankle flexion needed for a deep, knee-bent skating stance and a deep squat; adequate dorsiflexion lets the knee track forward for powerful push-off without compensating elsewhere.
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.cues: "Heel stays glued down" · "knee tracks over the toes" · "small steps back to progress"
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.mistakes: Heel lifting; knee caving inward; foot rolling to the inside
ankle-dorsiflexion-wall.progression: Progress: move foot farther from wall / add light load | Regress: foot closer to wall, smaller range

banded-monster-walk.name: Banded Monster Walk
banded-monster-walk.execution: Mini-band around ankles or above the knees. In an athletic quarter-squat, step diagonally forward-and-out with one foot, then the other, “walking” forward against constant tension. Keep the stance wide, toes forward, knees pushed out, chest tall. Walk forward a set number of steps, then backward.
banded-monster-walk.why: Maintains continuous tension on the hip abductors and glutes while resisting adduction in both the forward and lateral planes, building multi-directional hip stability and glute activation through a walking pattern.
banded-monster-walk.transfer: Activates the glutes and abductors that drive and stabilize push-off and crossovers; keeping the knees out under tension trains resistance to valgus collapse, protecting the knee on edges and turns.
banded-monster-walk.cues: "Knees out, toes forward" · "stay low, keep tension" · "wide steps"
banded-monster-walk.mistakes: Knees caving in; standing up tall; losing band tension between steps
banded-monster-walk.progression: Progress: heavier band or lower stance | Regress: lighter band, higher stance, fewer steps
banded-monster-walk.muscles: Gluteus medius, glute max, hip abductors

bodyweight-squat.name: Bodyweight Squat
bodyweight-squat.execution: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Brace the core, push the hips back and bend the knees, sitting down between the legs until the thighs reach at least parallel. Keep the heels flat, knees tracking over the toes, chest tall. Drive through the whole foot to stand, squeezing the glutes at the top.
bodyweight-squat.why: Grooves the fundamental knee- and hip-flexion squat pattern, building quad and glute strength and joint coordination through a full range — the foundation for all loaded squatting and jumping.
bodyweight-squat.transfer: Builds the deep knee-bend posture and leg strength underlying the skating stance and push-off; mastering the pattern transfers to powerful, repeatable stride extension and a stable athletic base.
bodyweight-squat.cues: "Sit between the legs" · "knees out over the toes" · "drive the floor away"
bodyweight-squat.mistakes: Heels lifting; knees caving inward; not reaching depth
bodyweight-squat.progression: Progress: 3-sec eccentric tempo or goblet load | Regress: squat to a box for depth control

goblet-squat-light-db.name: Goblet Squat (Light DB)
goblet-squat-light-db.execution: Hold a DB vertically against the chest, elbows tucked under it. Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Brace, push the hips back and squat to at least parallel, chest tall and elbows inside the knees. Drive through the whole foot to stand. Keep the weight close to the body throughout.
goblet-squat-light-db.why: The front-loaded weight acts as a counterbalance that encourages an upright torso and deeper range, increasing quad and glute loading while reinforcing a braced trunk and clean squat mechanics.
goblet-squat-light-db.transfer: Strengthens the knee-bent push-off musculature and trains the upright, braced posture of a strong skating stance; the anterior load reinforces the core stiffness used to hold position in battles.
goblet-squat-light-db.cues: "Elbows inside the knees" · "tall chest, weight on the chest" · "drive through mid-foot"
goblet-squat-light-db.mistakes: Chest collapsing forward; heels rising; knees caving in
goblet-squat-light-db.progression: Progress: heavier DB or bottom pause | Regress: lighter/no weight (bodyweight squat)
goblet-squat-light-db.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core

cossack-squat.name: Cossack Squat
cossack-squat.execution: Stand wide, feet ~1.5× shoulder width, toes slightly out. Shift onto one leg, bending that knee and sitting the hips down and back while the trailing leg stays straight with toes up. Keep the planted heel flat and chest tall; descend until the working thigh is near parallel, then drive through the heel back to center. Alternate.
cossack-squat.why: Loads the working hip into deep flexion and abduction while the trailing adductors lengthen under tension (eccentric), developing single-leg strength, frontal-plane control, and hip/ankle mobility through a long range a bilateral squat can’t train.
cossack-squat.transfer: Mirrors the wide, laterally loaded position of the stride and crossovers; strong, mobile adductors and single-leg control improve push-off power and protect against groin/hip strains, among the most common hockey injuries.
cossack-squat.cues: "Heel glued down" · "chest proud" · "sit between the legs, not forward"
cossack-squat.mistakes: Heel lifting; planted knee caving in; chest collapsing forward; not reaching honest depth
cossack-squat.progression: Progress: goblet DB or 3-sec eccentric | Regress: hold a pole/TRX or reduce depth

banded-front-squat.name: Banded Front Squat
banded-front-squat.execution: Stand on a long band, feet shoulder-width, and rack the band across the front of the shoulders (elbows high). Brace and squat to parallel, torso upright and elbows lifted. Drive up through the whole foot against increasing band tension. Keep the chest tall throughout.
banded-front-squat.why: Front-rack positioning enforces an upright torso and quad emphasis, while the band gives accommodating resistance — tension rises toward the top, matching the strength curve and increasing demand where you’re strongest.
banded-front-squat.transfer: Builds quad-dominant strength in an upright posture matching the skating stance, and the band’s top-end overload trains the forceful lockout that mirrors finishing a powerful stride extension.
banded-front-squat.cues: "Elbows high, chest tall" · "fight the band at the top" · "knees out, heels down"
banded-front-squat.mistakes: Elbows dropping (torso folds); rising onto the toes; cutting depth short
banded-front-squat.progression: Progress: heavier band or bottom pause | Regress: lighter band or bodyweight goblet squat

iso-wall-sit.name: Iso Wall Sit
iso-wall-sit.execution: Back flat against a wall, slide down until hips and knees are at ~90°, thighs parallel. Keep the feet flat and under the knees, back pressed to the wall, weight in the heels. Hold for the prescribed time, breathing steadily, then stand to finish.
iso-wall-sit.why: A sustained isometric hold builds quad strength-endurance and tendon stiffness under constant tension, training the muscles to resist fatigue at a fixed joint angle while teaching tolerance of a low, loaded posture.
iso-wall-sit.transfer: Develops the quad endurance and low, knee-bent posture-tolerance needed to hold an athletic skating stance through a long shift; builds isometric leg strength that supports stride position late in shifts.
iso-wall-sit.cues: "Thighs parallel, knees over ankles" · "press the whole back into the wall" · "breathe steadily"
iso-wall-sit.mistakes: Hips rising above knee height; knees drifting past the toes; holding the breath
iso-wall-sit.progression: Progress: DB on the lap or single-leg | Regress: shorter hold or higher knee angle

banded-squat.name: Banded Squat
banded-squat.execution: Stand on a band, feet shoulder-width, holding the other end at shoulder height (or looped over shoulders). Brace and squat to parallel, knees tracking over the toes, then drive up against the band. Keep the chest tall and heels down throughout; the band makes the top hardest.
banded-squat.why: Provides accommodating resistance that increases as you stand, overloading the lockout where leverage is best, while training the squat pattern and forceful hip/knee extension against rising tension.
banded-squat.transfer: Reinforces the squat-to-stand drive that mirrors stride extension, with the band’s top-end overload building the forceful finish of a push-off; a joint-friendly way to train extension power.
banded-squat.cues: "Knees out, heels down" · "explode against the band" · "tall chest"
banded-squat.mistakes: Knees caving; heels lifting; letting the band yank you down (losing control)
banded-squat.progression: Progress: heavier band or faster concentric | Regress: lighter band or bodyweight squat

deep-squat-hold.name: Deep Squat Hold
deep-squat-hold.execution: Lower into the bottom of a deep squat — hips below parallel — feet flat, heels down, knees pushed out. Keep the chest as tall as mobility allows and use the elbows to gently press the knees apart. Settle weight evenly through the feet and hold for the prescribed time, breathing into the position.
deep-squat-hold.why: Sustained time in deep flexion builds tissue tolerance and active strength at end range for the hips, knees, and ankles, reinforcing the ability to own a deep, stable bottom position rather than just passing through it.
deep-squat-hold.transfer: Develops the deep hip and ankle range and position-strength that support a low, powerful skating stance; greater end-range control improves stride depth and resilience of the hips and knees under deep loading.
deep-squat-hold.cues: "Heels down, knees out" · "tall as you can, chest up" · "breathe into the hips"
deep-squat-hold.mistakes: Heels lifting; rounding the low back; knees collapsing inward
deep-squat-hold.progression: Progress: longer hold or light goblet load | Regress: hold a support or elevate the heels slightly

glute-bridge.name: Glute Bridge
glute-bridge.execution: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width, arms at your sides. Brace the core and drive through the heels to lift the hips until the body is a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top, pause, then lower with control. Avoid arching the low back.
glute-bridge.why: Trains hip extension in isolation, teaching the glutes to produce extension force without the hamstrings or low back dominating; builds the glute strength and recruitment that underpin all hinging and push-off.
glute-bridge.transfer: Strengthens the glute-driven hip extension that powers the final phase of the stride; a strong, well-recruited glute improves push-off force and offloads the low back and hamstrings during skating.
glute-bridge.cues: "Drive through the heels" · "squeeze the glutes, ribs down" · "straight line, don’t over-arch"
glute-bridge.mistakes: Arching the low back instead of extending the hips; pushing through the toes; not reaching full extension
glute-bridge.progression: Progress: single-leg or barbell/DB across the hips | Regress: shorten range or add only a brief pause

band-glute-bridge.name: Band Glute Bridge
band-glute-bridge.execution: On your back, knees bent, feet flat, mini-band above the knees. Press the knees outward against the band. Drive through the heels to lift the hips into a straight line, squeezing the glutes at the top while maintaining outward knee pressure. Pause, then lower under control.
band-glute-bridge.why: Adds an abduction demand to the bridge, recruiting the gluteus medius alongside the glute max so the hips extend while resisting knee collapse — training hip extension and frontal-plane stability simultaneously.
band-glute-bridge.transfer: Builds the combined hip extension and abduction control used to push off and hold edges; keeping the knees driving out under load trains the valgus resistance that protects the knee on crossovers and turns.
band-glute-bridge.cues: "Knees press out the whole time" · "heels down, squeeze the glutes" · "ribs down, don’t arch"
band-glute-bridge.mistakes: Knees caving in (losing tension); over-arching the low back; pushing through the toes
band-glute-bridge.progression: Progress: single-leg banded bridge or hip load | Regress: lighter band or no band

sl-glute-bridge-band.name: SL Glute Bridge (Band)
sl-glute-bridge-band.execution: On your back, mini-band above the knees, one foot flat and the other leg extended or knee tucked. Press the working knee slightly out against the band, then drive through the planted heel to lift the hips level, squeezing the glute. Keep the pelvis square — don’t let it tip. Lower with control. Switch sides.
sl-glute-bridge-band.why: Combines single-leg hip extension with an anti-tilt/anti-rotation demand and band abduction, exposing side-to-side glute differences while building unilateral glute power and pelvic control.
sl-glute-bridge-band.transfer: Trains the one-leg glute drive and pelvic stability that match the single-leg nature of each skating push; correcting left-right asymmetries improves stride symmetry and reduces compensations that strain the low back and groin.
sl-glute-bridge-band.cues: "Hips stay level" · "knee presses out" · "all the drive through one heel"
sl-glute-bridge-band.mistakes: Pelvis tilting/dropping on the free side; arching the low back; pushing through the toes
sl-glute-bridge-band.progression: Progress: hip load or top pause | Regress: keep both feet down (band glute bridge)
sl-glute-bridge-band.muscles: Glute max, gluteus medius, hamstrings, core

db-rdl.name: DB RDL
db-rdl.execution: Hold DBs in front of the thighs, feet hip-width, knees softly bent. Brace and push the hips straight back, sliding the DBs down the front of the legs while keeping the back flat and the bells close. Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch around mid-shin, then drive the hips forward to stand, squeezing the glutes. Keep the shins near vertical.
db-rdl.why: Trains hip-hinge mechanics with heavy eccentric loading of the hamstrings and glutes through hip flexion; lengthening the posterior chain under tension builds hamstring strength and stiffness while reinforcing a neutral, braced spine.
db-rdl.transfer: Strengthens the glute/hamstring hip extension that finishes the stride push-off and builds posterior-chain strength that protects the low back and hamstrings during skating and sudden decelerations.
db-rdl.cues: "Hips back, not down" · "long flat back" · "drag the bells down the legs"
db-rdl.mistakes: Rounding the low back; turning it into a squat (knees travel forward); the DBs drifting away from the body
db-rdl.progression: Progress: heavier DBs or 3-sec eccentric | Regress: lighter load or reduce range (higher finish)

sl-db-rdl.name: SL DB RDL
sl-db-rdl.execution: Hold a DB in one or both hands and stand on one leg with a soft knee. Hinge at the hip, extending the free leg straight behind as the torso lowers and the DB tracks toward the floor; keep the hips square and back flat. Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch, then drive the hip forward to return to standing. Reps, then switch.
sl-db-rdl.why: Combines hip-hinge eccentric hamstring loading with a strong anti-rotation and balance demand on one leg, building unilateral posterior-chain strength and the hip/ankle stability needed to control the pelvis.
sl-db-rdl.transfer: Trains the single-leg hip extension and pelvic control underlying each skating stride, improving push-off balance and stride symmetry while building hamstring resilience and ankle/hip stability for edge control.
sl-db-rdl.cues: "Hips square, don’t open" · "reach the back heel to the wall" · "flat back, slow down"
sl-db-rdl.mistakes: Hips rotating open; rounding the back; rushing and losing balance
sl-db-rdl.progression: Progress: heavier DB or eyes closed | Regress: lighter/no weight or tap the back toe down for balance
sl-db-rdl.muscles: Hamstrings, glutes, hip stabilizers, erectors, core
sl-db-rdl.nameHint: Румынская тяга на одной ноге с гантелью

banded-rdl.name: Banded RDL
banded-rdl.execution: Stand on a band, feet hip-width, holding the other end at the hips or shoulders. Soft knees, brace, push the hips straight back against rising band tension, keeping the back flat. Lower to a hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand against the band. Keep the band path close to the body.
banded-rdl.why: The band provides accommodating resistance — tension peaks at lockout — overloading the top of the hip hinge where the glutes finish extension, while training the hinge pattern with a joint-friendly stimulus.
banded-rdl.transfer: Builds the forceful end-range glute/hamstring extension that finishes the stride push-off; the top-end band overload mirrors the powerful hip snap at full stride extension.
banded-rdl.cues: "Hips back, fight the band up" · "flat back" · "snap the hips through at the top"
banded-rdl.mistakes: Rounding the back; squatting instead of hinging; letting the band pull you out of position
banded-rdl.progression: Progress: heavier band or pause at the stretch | Regress: lighter band or shorter range

sl-rdl-banded.name: SL RDL (Banded)
sl-rdl-banded.execution: Anchor a band underfoot of the standing leg (or to the working hip) and stand on one leg. Hinge at the hip, free leg extending behind, lowering against band tension to a hamstring stretch with a flat back and square hips. Drive the hip forward to stand against the band. Reps, then switch.
sl-rdl-banded.why: Marries single-leg hinge mechanics and balance with accommodating band resistance that peaks at the top, building unilateral posterior-chain strength, pelvic stability, and a forceful end-range hip extension.
sl-rdl-banded.transfer: Strengthens the single-leg, end-range hip extension specific to each skating push while training the pelvic control that keeps the stride efficient; resilient hamstrings reduce strain risk on hard pushes.
sl-rdl-banded.cues: "Hips square, drive through one heel" · "flat back" · "finish tall against the band"
sl-rdl-banded.mistakes: Hips rotating open; back rounding; balance breaking down under tension
sl-rdl-banded.progression: Progress: heavier band or top hold | Regress: lighter band or touch the back toe for balance

banded-hamstring-slides.name: Banded Hamstring Slides
banded-hamstring-slides.execution: Lie on your back, heels on sliders or a towel, optionally with a band adding tension. Bridge the hips up, then slide the heels out by straightening the legs while keeping the hips lifted, then curl the heels back in toward the glutes under control. Keep the hips high throughout.
banded-hamstring-slides.why: Loads the hamstrings eccentrically as the legs straighten (lengthening under tension) and concentrically on the curl back, training knee-flexion hamstring strength and eccentric control — a key protector against hamstring strain.
banded-hamstring-slides.transfer: Builds eccentric hamstring strength and control that protects against the strains common in explosive skating and sprinting, and supports the knee-flexion/leg-recovery phase of the stride.
banded-hamstring-slides.cues: "Hips stay high" · "slide out slow, curl in strong" · "control the stretch"
banded-hamstring-slides.mistakes: Hips dropping as the legs extend; rushing the eccentric; using the low back instead of the hamstrings
banded-hamstring-slides.progression: Progress: add band resistance or single-leg | Regress: smaller range or feet-on-floor curls
banded-hamstring-slides.nameHint: Сгибание ног со скольжением с эспандером

reverse-lunge.name: Reverse Lunge
reverse-lunge.execution: From standing, step one foot back and lower until both knees reach ~90°, front shin vertical, torso upright, back knee hovering just off the floor. Keep weight in the front heel. Drive through the front foot to return to standing. Alternate or complete reps per side. Keep the core braced and hips square.
reverse-lunge.why: Loads the front leg in a single-leg pattern with less knee shear than a forward lunge; the backward step emphasizes glute and hamstring loading and builds unilateral strength, balance, and frontal-plane control.
reverse-lunge.transfer: Develops the single-leg strength and stability behind each stride push-off; the split stance trains balance and the deceleration control used when stopping and changing direction.
reverse-lunge.cues: "Step back, drop straight down" · "front shin vertical, weight in the heel" · "tall chest"
reverse-lunge.mistakes: Front knee caving in or shooting past the toes; leaning forward; short step (knee over-bends)
reverse-lunge.progression: Progress: hold DBs or add a pause | Regress: hold a support or reduce depth

walking-lunge.name: Walking Lunge
walking-lunge.execution: Step forward into a lunge, lowering until both knees reach ~90° with the front shin vertical. Drive through the front foot and step the back foot through into the next lunge, traveling forward. Keep the torso upright and core braced, controlling each descent. Continue for distance or reps.
walking-lunge.why: Trains single-leg strength through a full range while moving, demanding dynamic balance, hip and knee control, and coordination as the body translates forward over the lead leg — building unilateral leg strength under locomotion.
walking-lunge.transfer: Mirrors the forward propulsion and single-leg loading of skating; builds the leg strength and dynamic balance that support stride power and stability as the body moves over each push leg.
walking-lunge.cues: "Long step, drop down not forward" · "front shin tall" · "control the landing"
walking-lunge.mistakes: Short, knee-dominant steps; torso pitching forward; front knee caving inward
walking-lunge.progression: Progress: hold DBs or add a deficit | Regress: in-place reverse lunge or hold a support

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
bulgarian-split-squat.execution: Stand a stride in front of a bench, lacing the top of the rear foot on it. Brace and lower the back knee toward the floor by bending the front leg, keeping the front shin fairly vertical and torso slightly forward. Descend until the front thigh is near parallel, then drive through the front foot to stand. Reps, then switch.
bulgarian-split-squat.why: Elevating the rear foot shifts the load heavily onto the front leg, building deep single-leg quad/glute strength and stability through a long range with a strong balance and hip-control demand.
bulgarian-split-squat.transfer: Directly overloads single-leg push-off strength specific to skating; deep front-leg loading builds stride power and the unilateral stability that supports edges, turns, and resilience of the knee and hip.
bulgarian-split-squat.cues: "Down toward the floor, not forward" · "weight in the front heel" · "tall torso, control the descent"
bulgarian-split-squat.mistakes: Front knee caving; standing too close (knee jams forward); rushing the eccentric
bulgarian-split-squat.progression: Progress: hold DBs or add a pause/tempo | Regress: lower the elevation or do a split squat (rear foot down)

db-goblet-lateral-lunge.name: DB Goblet Lateral Lunge
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.execution: Hold a DB at the chest (goblet). Step wide to one side, bending that knee and pushing the hips back while the trailing leg stays straight, both feet flat and toes forward. Descend until the working thigh nears parallel, chest tall, then drive back to center. Reps, then switch sides.
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.why: Loads the working hip into flexion and abduction while the straight-leg adductors lengthen under tension, building frontal-plane single-leg strength, adductor strength, and lateral hip mobility under load.
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.transfer: Trains the lateral loading and push of the stride and crossovers; strong, mobile adductors loaded in this exact plane improve push-off power and protect against the common groin/hip strains.
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.cues: "Sit the hips back, heel down" · "tall chest, weight on the chest" · "push back to center"
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.mistakes: Heel lifting on the working side; chest collapsing forward; knee caving in
db-goblet-lateral-lunge.progression: Progress: heavier DB or pause at depth | Regress: bodyweight or reduce depth
